PullRequest.Title: Sessions: Add #file context completions to new-chat input
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/299057
Adds `#` completions to the sessions `NewChatViewPane` input editor, scoped to the workspace selected in the dropdown picker.

## Changes

### New file: `variableCompletions.ts`
- `VariableCompletionHandler` registers a completion provider on the `sessions-chat` URI scheme (same pattern as `SlashCommandHandler`)
- Typing `#` immediately shows files from the selected workspace
- For `file://` and `vscodeRemote` schemes: uses `ISearchService.fileSearch()`
- For virtual schemes (e.g. `github-remote-file://`): walks the file tree via `IFileService.resolve()`
- Recent workspace-scoped files from editor history (`IHistoryService`) are always shown
- Accepted completions insert `#file:<name>` text with slash-command-style decorations (colored background/foreground via `chatSlashCommandForeground`/`chatSlashCommandBackground`, rounded corners)
- Files are also added as attachment pills via `NewChatContextAttachments`

### Modified: `newChatContextAttachments.ts`
- Added public `addAttachments()` method (wraps private `_addAttachments()`)

### Modified: `newChatViewPane.ts`
- Imported and instantiated `VariableCompletionHandler` alongside `SlashCommandHandler`
- Passes the editor, context attachments, and workspace URI getter

## Design decisions
- **No `@` completions** — only `#` for file context, matching what makes sense for the sessions pre-chat state
- **No `#sym:`, `#selection`, `#session`** — symbols require open editors/language servers (unavailable pre-session), selection/session don't apply in the sessions app
- **Workspace-scoped** — all results filtered to the workspace selected in the dropdown, matching the "Add Context..." button behavior
- **No core dependencies added** — all code lives in `vs/sessions/`, imports only from allowed layers

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call, empty-pattern expansion, absence of a result bound/cache key, sorted-search implementation, and incomplete-provider re-trigger path are all directly traced. Exact wall time varies with repository size and filesystem speed, but the full-scan and per-prefix multiplicity are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem enumeration/search-process CPU plus arrays and completion objects for up to 20,000 file results and derived folders.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(F) filesystem enumeration plus scoring/allocation for workspace file count F on bare `#`, multiplied by the number of typed completion prefixes because no cache key is reused.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked completion latency with repeated I/O, CPU, and GC pressure while typing.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, typing `#` in the sessions new-chat editor did not start file search. The existing workbench chat completion implementation shows history for an empty pattern and, once a pattern exists, reuses a search cache key across prefixes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new completion provider always calls searchFilesAndFolders, including for a bare `#`, and passes no cache key; because its list is marked incomplete, subsequent typed characters invoke the provider again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 254 invokes `searchFilesAndFolders(workspaceUri, pattern || '', ..., undefined, ...)`, newly placing an empty, uncached workspace search on the `#` completion path.
Findings.Title: Avoid uncached full-workspace searches for `#` completions
Findings.Impact: In a large local or vscode-remote repository, merely typing `#` can scan and score the whole workspace before suggestions appear; continuing to type repeats the scan, causing delayed completions, high filesystem/search-process CPU, and allocation/GC pressure during normal input.
Findings.Evidence: At line 254, `pattern || ''` turns bare `#` into an empty fuzzy search and the `undefined` cache key disables search reuse. `searchFilesAndFolders` converts the empty pattern to `*`, sets `sortByScore: true`, and specifies no `maxResults`; the raw search path walks all candidates before selecting up to the 20,000-result default. `result.incomplete = true` at line 158 causes SuggestModel to re-trigger incomplete providers as the cursor advances, so each prefix starts another uncached filesystem/search-provider traversal. The core chat analogue guards the search with `if (pattern)` and supplies `updateCacheKey().key`.
Findings.Recommendation: Match the existing chat provider: return history-only suggestions for an empty pattern, keep a short-lived per-handler search cache key for non-empty prefixes and clear it on disposal/expiry, and set an explicit completion-sized result bound.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The recursive call count, match-dependent stopping condition, serial awaits, file-service cancellation limitation, and GitHub provider's full-map `readdir` implementation are directly traced. Repository shape controls duration, but large repositories with unmatched prefixes are a realistic trigger.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One cold recursive-tree network response, D serial file-service resolves, and repeated renderer-thread scans over F cached tree entries.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a query with fewer than 100 matches, resolves scale with all reachable directories D (depth at most 10); in `github-remote-file`, warm CPU work scales as O(D×F) because each `readdir` scans the F-entry tree map.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Severe completion latency and renderer CPU blocking, potentially making input appear frozen.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, typing in the sessions new-chat input never traversed a virtual workspace. A similar pre-existing walk was reachable only after explicitly opening the attachment picker; the diff newly moves it onto completion retrieval while typing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For virtual workspaces, the new typing-triggered completion recursively calls `IFileService.resolve` once per directory and stops only after collecting 100 matching suggestions, reaching every directory up to depth 10 when a selective pattern has few or no matches.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 295 places `await this.fileService.resolve(uri)` in a newly recursive completion walk invoked from the added provider; this boundary did not exist on the editor typing path before the diff.
Findings.Title: Bound virtual-workspace traversal independently of matches
Findings.Impact: After typing a selective `#` query in a large GitHub remote repository, the suggestion request can perform thousands of serial resolves and repeated full-tree scans, freezing or severely delaying the new-chat UI; a cold cache also waits for the full recursive GitHub tree request.
Findings.Evidence: Line 295 is inside `collect`, which recursively awaits itself for every child directory at line 311. The 100-result guard counts matches rather than visited directories, so a miss visits D directories serially. For the sessions `github-remote-file` provider, the first resolve fetches the entire recursive GitHub tree over the network, and each directory `readdir` then iterates every entry in that cached tree; this makes a warm traversal O(D×F), with the synchronous map scans occurring in the renderer. `resolve` has no cancellation token, so cancellation is only observed between directory calls.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not recursively enumerate the virtual tree on each completion request. Use a cancellable cached/indexed search where available, or constrain completion work with a visited-directory/time budget independent of match count and show recent/top-level entries until a more explicit search; coalesce/cache the index per workspace.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type `#` and continue a file-completion query in a selected local or vscode-remote workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion provider awaits history filtering and `searchFilesAndFolders`; suggestions cannot be returned until file search, scoring, folder derivation, and completion-item creation finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sorted file search enumerates workspace files and derives matching folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One search per completion invocation; bare `#` scans F files, and incomplete completions repeat for each typed prefix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Typing in the sessions input performed no file search. The analogous workbench chat provider skips search for an empty pattern and reuses a cache key for non-empty prefixes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider awaits the complete search before returning any suggestions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Desktop file search can dispatch enumeration/scoring to the search process/provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per uncached completion query; internal work scales with F.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No search-process request was on this sessions editor typing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion waits for the search result and sorting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the selected workspace's file count F. Bare `#` matches the workspace broadly and sorted search enumerates all candidates before retaining up to the 20,000 default; each later prefix causes another uncached traversal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Monaco cancels the preceding suggest request when retriggering, but each incomplete prefix starts a fresh search with no shared cache key or coalescing. There is normally one current request, with possible cancellation overlap while the prior search provider unwinds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No completion/search cache is supplied. OS/provider warm state may reduce physical I/O, but filesystem enumeration, matching, scoring, folder derivation, and object allocation repeat. Cancellation is not a reusable positive or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added call, empty-pattern expansion, sorted-search behavior, absent cache key, and incomplete-provider retrigger are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Wall time depends on repository size, excludes, provider, and filesystem warmth; large monorepos make the full-scan cost substantial.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity repeated I/O/CPU regression: bare `#` and subsequent prefixes trigger unbounded, uncached workspace searches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type a selective `#` completion query in a selected github-remote-file virtual workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider awaits the depth-first recursive walk. A selective miss cannot return until every reachable directory up to depth 10 has been resolved or cancellation is noticed between resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the full recursive repository tree from the GitHub Trees API on first access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold request per owner/repo/ref within the five-minute provider cache window, coalesced if already in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This network operation existed for the virtual filesystem, but typing in the sessions input did not place it on the completion path; only explicit repository/file interactions could trigger it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold completion request waits for authentication, network response, JSON parsing, and full-tree indexing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve every traversed virtual directory and enumerate its direct children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D serial resolves for a selective miss or fewer than 100 matches, bounded only by depth 10 and cancellation checks between calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No virtual-directory traversal occurred while typing. A similar traversal was confined to the explicitly opened attachment picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All resolves complete serially before suggestions return; resolve itself has no cancellation token.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: For fewer than 100 matches, effective cardinality is D reachable directories. In the GitHub provider each directory readdir scans the cached F-entry recursive tree, producing O(D×F) renderer CPU work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Directory traversal is explicitly serialized by `await collect` inside the loop. GitHub tree network fetches are coalesced per repository, but no limiter/cache avoids repeated per-directory resolution and map scans within a completion request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The GitHub provider positively caches a full tree for five minutes, negatively caches 404s for one minute, and coalesces in-flight fetches. Warm cache removes network latency but not the D repeated full-map scans; completion results/indexes are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: recursive serial resolves, match-count stopping, provider cache behavior, and the provider's per-directory full-map readdir are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact D and F depend on repository shape and depth; large GitHub repositories make the quadratic-like scan realistic and severe.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity boundary fan-out and renderer CPU regression on selective virtual-workspace completion queries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accept a file/folder completion and render the resulting attachment and input decoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion command adds one attachment, updates attachment rendering/events, and the editor content-change listener rescans the short chat input for `#file:` decorations. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is required on acceptance.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Attachment duplicate checks scale with the small attached-context count A; decoration scanning scales with chat input length and number of references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-item command and rendering updates; no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the accepted attachment. Decoration type registration is static and performed once; per-widget listeners are disposed with the handler.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the command, attachment mutation, and decoration update call paths are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Input and attachment lists are normally small; no evidence shows realistic sizes that make these local scans a performance regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance issue; the local acceptance/rendering work is bounded in the expected workflow.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all three changed files and relevant transitive search, suggest, file-service, and GitHub virtual-filesystem paths. Submitted two high-confidence findings: repeated uncached full-workspace search on local/remote completion input, and match-dependent serial virtual-tree traversal with repeated full-tree scans.
